findings.text: `toBag_rank` says ORDER BY without LIMIT is invisible to any outer query, but the theorem proves only that sorting preserves the bag, and probes P11 and P12 show readers that observe the order. Fix: restrict the claim to total sort keys and readers whose result depends only on the bag.

The docstring says an all-tied ranking has one group, but `rank` produces zero groups for empty input and the theorem establishes equality of permitted lists in both cases. Fix: state that nonempty input produces one group and empty input permits only the empty list.

The docstring gives SQLite `min` and `max` as examples of permutation-invariant functions, but the pinned SQLite returns `a` or `A` for both aggregates under `NOCASE` depending on which value comes first. Fix: use `count` as the example or require that tied extrema have identical result values.

The docstring calls projection after LIMIT SQLite’s clause order, although the prototype can defer projection because `project` is a total function and `le` already compares input rows. Fix: describe this as the prototype’s evaluation order and state those assumptions in the module and README descriptions as well.

`exists_perm_of_perm_map` has a proof of more than 20 lines and its docstring gives only the conclusion. Fix: explain how induction on the permutation lifts each swap to the source list even when the projection maps different rows to the same value.

`first_group_varies` has a proof of more than 20 lines and no proof sketch. Fix: explain how exchanging two distinct rows across the prefix boundary gives two permitted lists with different prefix bags.

`equivalent_but_canonical_results_differ` has a proof of more than 20 lines and no proof sketch. Fix: explain that both results permit exactly the two row orders and that group sizes distinguish their canonical rankings.

`window_ofBag_iff` has a proof of more than 50 lines and its docstring gives only the result. Fix: explain why a zero-size slice yields the empty bag and how `Bag.take_iff` characterizes every remaining case.
